title: Native Sessions journal, accepted facts, and owner delivery
alt: Projects & Config validates current permission and accepted run selection. Events & Sessions pins the journal, commits accepted facts, and serves ordered replay. After a fresh authority check and owner CAS, the Orchestrator commits the trusted accepted-run Sandbox binding with the winning plan decision, gate, grants, and outbox (its adapter only resolves existing resources), persists owner receipts and fenced message delivery; generic PolicyEvaluation append remains denied until #1846's trusted consumer.

steps.label: POST /internal/sessions/{sessionId}
OpenIddict validates issuer/audience; host requires GUID sub and one active project/run grant.
Resolve default or permitted project override
Runtime uses password-free workload identity and verifies schema only; --migrate uses a separate privileged identity.
Verify owned schema; negotiate live database identity
Confirm database and resource generation
Return exact provider, options revision, resource, and capabilities
Persist immutable project/run pin and session
Commit; return SessionRecord
201 Created
Later append, replay, and subscribe verify the exact stored pin; changed or missing bindings fail closed.
POST /internal/sessions/{sessionId}/events
Generic PolicyEvaluation append fails closed: actor=sub/run scope do not prove Core provenance; #1846 receipt consumer is not wired.
Verify run pin; atomically write event, refs, sequence, and outbox
Commit before returning durable event
201 new event; 200 identical retry
GET /internal/projects/{projectId}/runs/{runId}/events[/live]
Read durable events after cursor; poll for live subscription
Rows retain session identity
Page or NDJSON: event + opaque nextCursor
Knowledge receipts are project facts, not session events. Orchestrator validates its owner outbox before fenced turn-boundary delivery; receipt is not approval.
The separate mapped runtime-owner-context read rechecks the latest root decision and Projects authority; changed state returns 409.
